description: This pie chart depicts the distribution of emotion categories within the IEMOCAP dataset. The chart contains six slices, each representing a different emotion: Frustration, Neutral, Anger, Sadness, Excitement, and Happiness. The slice representing Frustration is light blue and occupies approximately 25.1% of the chart, while Neutral, in blue, represents 23.1%. Anger is shown in yellow and accounts for roughly 14.9%, followed by Sadness in orange at 14.7%. Excitement is represented by a red slice at approximately 14.1%, and Happiness, in pink, occupies about 8.1% of the chart. Percentage labels are displayed within each slice, and the slices appear to be ordered clockwise, with the largest slices positioned first and decreasing in size as they proceed around the circle. A legend is not present, but each slice is labeled directly outside of the pie chart.
caption_used: The pie chart illustrates the distribution of emotion categories in the IEMOCAP dataset, with percentages displayed relative to the number of utterances. Frustration is the largest category, accounting for approximately 25.1% of the data, followed by Neutral at 23.1%. Anger and Sadness are nearly equal, with Anger slightly higher at 15.9% and Sadness at 14.7%. Excitement and Happiness are the smallest categories, with Happiness at 10.1% and Excitement at 14.1%. Notably, the data suggests a consistent decline in positive emotions (Excitement and Happiness) compared to negative ones (Frustration, Anger, and Sadness). The chart provides a clear visual representation of the emotional distribution, with labels positioned outside each slice for clarity.
